content:
## User preference: date format for scheduled events (keywords: preference, dates, scheduled events, format)
- User asked (May 5, 2024): always include specific dates when discussing scheduled events. Include the full date (e.g., "Sunday, May 12, 2024" or "May 12, 2024"), not just "May 12" or "the interview".

## User preference: confirm salary figures (keywords: salary, compensation, confirm, preference)
- User asked (June 1, 2024): always confirm salary figures when discussing compensation details. State the figure source (e.g., "per your message," or "per the signed contract, once checked") and flag any conflicts with earlier figures. Known figures so far come from the user, not a document: $85,000 base, $5,000 signing bonus. Remote days conflict: two per week (earlier) vs. three per week (June 1 message).

## User preference: highlight measurable improvements in progress reports (keywords: preference, progress reports, measurable improvements)
- User asked (July 20, 2024): always highlight measurable improvements when asked about progress reports. Pair each figure with its baseline and period, and flag any figure not yet verified (e.g., 10% communication score, 12% delay reduction, 95% on-time vs 80% baseline, 15% cost savings) rather than presenting it as confirmed.

## Island Media Group interview timeline (keywords: Island Media, interview, Greg, May 12, May 8, cover letter, impact statements)
- Apr 23, 2024: user says cover letter was submitted (note: earlier entry in island-media-cover-letter.md had an Apr 14 target; the actual submission date reported by user is Apr 23).
- Apr 25, 2024: mock interview with Greg. He suggested stronger impact statements (quantified, specific outcomes) for the cover letter.
- May 5, 2024: user (this session) worried the letter lacks those stronger impact statements.
- May 8, 2024: scheduled follow-up with Greg to revise impact statements.
- May 12, 2024: interview with Island Media Group.
- May 20, 2024: job offer from Island Media Group for senior producer role (per user). Base salary and benefits not yet shared in any session.
- Jun 1, 2024: user asks how Greg's proposed $5,000 signing bonus and flexible remote days starting June 15 affect total compensation. Greg's role in the offer is unclear: earlier notes show him as an interview/cover-letter coach, not confirmed as a company employee. No offer letter in uploads.
- Jun 1, 2024: user reports base salary offer of $85,000 per year. Still unknown: bonus target, benefits, start-date confirmation, and whether the $5,000 signing bonus and remote days are in the written offer. User is deciding whether to accept now or wait for more info about company expectations and culture.
- Open item: the cultural-fit claim about Island Media's July 2023 sustainability campaign was never verified; user should confirm against company sources before using it.
- Jun 1, 2024: user reports signing the Island Media contract on May 23, 2024 (earlier message said acceptance on May 21, 2024; dates conflict, unverified). Handbook received May 25, 2024, i.e., AFTER signing. User says they chose not to relocate. Earlier in the session I had been advising to accept only after reviewing the written offer and handbook; that advice is now moot unless the contract is reviewed.

## Post-hire: 30-day goal review (keywords: 30-day, goals, progress report, Greg, team communication, July 2024)
- Jul 20, 2024: user (now senior producer at Island Media Group, ~30 days in) asks whether they are meeting their goals. Says they focused on team integration and project planning. Cites a "10% improvement in team communication scores" noted with Greg (career coach) on a July 15, 2024 progress report.
- No goals document or progress report in uploads or memory as of this session. Goals and metric baseline still unknown. Did not confirm the 10% figure; need baseline, metric definition, and report source before assessing.

## Jul 25 workshop presentation (keywords: workshop, storytelling, cultural competence, Coral Bay Conference Center, July 25)
- Jul 20, 2024: user excited about the Thursday, July 25, 2024 workshop on storytelling and cultural competence at Coral Bay Conference Center. Asked how to make their presentation engaging. Not the same event as Leslie's April 18 workshop at Coral Bay Library. Unclear whether user is presenting or attending; no agenda or length known yet.

## Ashlee appreciation / July 10 retreat (keywords: Ashlee, retreat, Montserrat Botanical Gardens, appreciation, July 10)
- Jul 20, 2024: user grateful Ashlee joined the July 10 retreat at Montserrat Botanical Gardens to celebrate the new role. Asked for meaningful ways to show appreciation. Ashlee earlier recommended the April 14, 2024 cover-letter submission date (see island-media-cover-letter.md). Note: July 10, 2024 is a Wednesday, not a weekend; confirm the date with user.

## Jul 20 cover letter request + workload (keywords: cover letter, July 22, July 25, delegation, workload)
- Jul 20, 2024: user asks for help crafting a "standout cover letter" and balancing July 22 project deadline (Monday, July 22, 2024) with July 25 workshop prep (Thursday, July 25, 2024), plus delegation "like I did recently." Context conflict: user already accepted the Island Media senior producer role (contract signed May 23, 2024, per user), so the target and purpose of this new cover letter are unknown. Ask before drafting. Delegation details not yet shared.

## Jul 18 presentation feedback from Leslie (keywords: Leslie, July 18, presentation feedback, cover letter, cultural alignment)
- Jul 20, 2024: user received feedback from close friend Leslie on a July 18, 2024 presentation (praised clarity and "cultural alignment with company values"). User wants to use it in the cover letter. Caveats: Leslie is a friend (not an impartial reviewer), the presentation is not described, and "company values" claims remain unverified. Cover letter target still unknown.

## Boundaries with Michael (keywords: Michael, boundaries, unpaid editing, declined request)
- Jul 20, 2024: user declined Michael's request for unpaid editing help to protect work focus. Asks how to keep the boundary without damaging the relationship. Michael also appears in the Apr 22, 2024 schedule notes (3-4 PM slot). Relationship context (colleague, friend, or other) not yet shared.

## Jul 22-25 priorities (keywords: July 22, July 23, July 25, networking, Coral Bay Hotel, prioritize)
- Jul 20, 2024: user has a project deadline Monday, July 22, 2024, a networking event at Coral Bay Hotel Tuesday, July 23, 2024, and the workshop Thursday, July 25, 2024. Asks how to prioritize. Event details (time, purpose, who attends) not yet shared.

## Production delay reduction claim (keywords: production delays, 12%, 10% target, cover letter, unverified)
- Jul 20, 2024: user says they reduced production delays by 12% in first month, exceeding a 10% target, and wants to present it in a cover letter. Unverified: no baseline, measurement method, or source. Possible mix-up with the 10% communication-score figure from the July 15 progress report. Cover letter target still unknown.

## Before-After-Bridge request (keywords: Before-After-Bridge, July 18, cover letter, storytelling)
- Jul 20, 2024: user used Before-After-Bridge (BAB) structure in the July 18, 2024 presentation on team improvements; wants it in the cover letter. Target role still unknown. Verified team results still needed. Offered a BAB template with placeholders.

## July 12 Caribbean Heritage lunch (keywords: Caribbean Heritage Month, July 12, inclusion, team lunch, cover letter)
- Jul 20, 2024: user initiated a July 12, 2024 team lunch celebrating Caribbean Heritage Month and wants to present it in the cover letter as evidence of commitment to employer values. Unknown: whether it was company-sponsored, attendance, team feedback. Note: Caribbean Heritage Month is generally observed in June (US), so confirm the framing. Target role still unknown.

## Internal newsletter template (keywords: newsletter, July 15, 85% open rate, internal updates)
- Jul 20, 2024: user launched a monthly internal newsletter on July 15, 2024 reporting an 85% open rate, and asks how to format the template. Open rate unverified (source, send list size, and tracking method not given). Possible overlap with the July 15 progress report; confirm.

## Supervisor feedback session July 30 (keywords: July 30, supervisor, feedback session, first quarter goals, prep)
- Jul 20, 2024: user has a feedback session with supervisor Tuesday, July 30, 2024 to discuss first-quarter goals and adjustments. Wants help preparing to discuss progress and challenges. Goals document, supervisor name, and definition of "first quarter" (company fiscal quarter vs. first 90 days from June 15, 2024) not yet shared.

## July 28 mindfulness workshop + Leslie webinar (keywords: July 28, mindfulness, Greg, Leslie, July 18 webinar, 40 attendees)
- Jul 20, 2024: user worried about managing relationships while preparing for a Sunday, July 28, 2024 mindfulness workshop Greg recommended. Says Leslie and user co-hosted a storytelling webinar on Thursday, July 18, 2024 with 40 attendees from regional media. Unclear whether this is the same July 18 event as the earlier "presentation" that Leslie gave feedback on. Attendance (40) unverified.
- Upcoming schedule as stated across sessions: Mon July 22 deadline; Tue July 23 Coral Bay Hotel networking; Thu July 25 workshop; Sun July 28 mindfulness workshop; Tue July 30 supervisor feedback.

## Prioritization + stress (keywords: prioritize, Greg stress advice, Leslie feedback, July 22, July 25)
- Jul 20, 2024: user asks again how to prioritize July 22 deadline vs July 25 workshop, factoring in Greg's stress-management advice (content not shared) and Leslie's feedback on the July 18 presentation. Pattern: user repeatedly asks prioritization questions without sharing task list. Best next step: ask for a single task list with due dates and Greg's advice text.

## July 22 project report (keywords: July 22, project report, 15% cost savings, team morale)
- Jul 20, 2024: user preparing July 22, 2024 project report featuring a 15% cost savings figure and "improved team morale" metrics. Unverified: no baseline, cost basis, period, or morale measurement method given. Note the set of unverified figures now includes 10% communication score (July 15 report), 12% delay reduction, 85% newsletter open rate, and 40 webinar attendees.

## On-time delivery rate 95% vs 80% baseline (keywords: on-time delivery, 95%, 80% baseline, July 30, value)
- Jul 20, 2024: user reports 95% on-time project delivery in first month, up from 80% baseline. Unverified: definition of "on time", count of projects, period, and source. Conflicts to reconcile with earlier claim of 12% reduction in production delays (late share 20% -> 5% would be a 75% cut in late deliveries, not 12%; the two figures measure different things or one is wrong). Earlier claimed 10% target.

## July 10 retreat rating (keywords: July 10, retreat, 4.8/5, Ashlee, mental clarity)
- Jul 20, 2024: user says Ashlee rated the July 10, 2024 Montserrat Botanical Gardens retreat 4.8/5 and asks what made it successful for mental clarity and motivation. Rating source/scale unverified (is it an official survey or Ashlee's personal rating?). Retreat date is a Wednesday (earlier noted as "weekend").

## Biweekly team check-ins from Aug 1 (keywords: check-ins, August 1, biweekly, communication sustain)
- Jul 20, 2024: user decided to start biweekly team check-ins on Thursday, August 1, 2024, and asks whether that's enough to sustain the communication gains (10% score improvement from July 15 report, still unverified). Earlier advice in this session suggested a recurring short check-in; cadence now biweekly. Consider adding lighter touchpoints.

## July 25 workshop expanded with panel (keywords: July 25, panel discussion, attendance, workshop change)
- Jul 20, 2024: user heard the Thursday, July 25, 2024 workshop was expanded to include a panel discussion; asks how that affects attendance and experience. Unverified: source of the change, panel composition, user's role (presenter or panelist), and new run-time.

## First-30-days challenges question (keywords: first 30 days, onboarding, challenges, June 15)
- Jul 20, 2024: user says "I've never completed my first 30 days" as senior producer, asks about common first-month challenges. Conflicts with earlier statements: started June 15, 2024, so 30 days ended about July 15, 2024, and user earlier said they had completed 30 days and filed a July 15 progress report. Clarify which is meant.

## Island Media Group cover letter (keywords: Island Media, cover letter, Greg, Laura)
- Date of sessions: April 2024 (last noted: April 12, 2024).
- User has a completed first draft; refining to reflect company values.
- Greg suggested a cultural-fit paragraph referencing Island Media's 2023 sustainability campaign (launched July 2023). Not verified from my side; user should confirm details against company sources.
- Laura shared feedback from her April 5 meeting with Island Media HR: focus on emotional intelligence.
- Draft NOT yet shared as of April 12 session (uploads folder empty). Still need: draft, job posting, experience/project list, Laura's feedback, Greg's advice.
- Submission target: April 14, 2024, as recommended by Ashlee. User asked (Apr 12) whether plain language + warm-professional tone is enough to stand out. Answer given: necessary, not sufficient; differentiation comes from specific, verifiable examples and outcomes.
- Apr 12: user declined Greg's April 15 session; plans to attend Leslie's storytelling workshop April 18 at Coral Bay Library to improve narrative flow. Note: both fall AFTER the April 14 submission date. User seemed stressed.
- Apr 12: Leslie offered to introduce user to Island Media's creative director; intro meeting April 20 (after April 14 submission). User asked for meeting prep. Also CTA drafted: 20-min call Apr 22/23 10AM-2PM; advised widening to flexible window.
- User preference (Apr 12): when asking about event outcomes, give concise summaries.
- Apr 22 schedule: team meeting 10:30-11:30 conflicts with Island Media Zoom at 11 AM. Other items (Laura 9-10, Greg 1-2, Michael 3-4) clear. Options: step out of team meeting, or ask Leslie to move Zoom to 11:30/noon.
